name: William Creek
reason: Town with its own Wikivoyage page and flindersandoutback.com.au town page; the William Creek Hotel pub is a named stop on the Oodnadatta Track (rule 1, 2)
objection: Tiny settlement, mainly a pub and airstrip; the visit is a meal and a photo

name: Cadney Homestead
reason: Roadhouse/business; Wikivoyage mentions it as an oasis stop only (rule 2: shop/restaurant)
objection: Wikivoyage calls it a nice surprise on the highway and it is the gateway to the Painted Desert

name: Mungerannie
reason: Outback pub and roadhouse on the Birdsville Track known for its memorabilia, a quirky roadside icon; only one counted source (flindersandoutback region page)
objection: It is a roadhouse and accommodation business and the source gives little to see

name: Oodnadatta Track
reason: Wikivoyage itinerary page gives the 617 km track its own article with sidings, mound springs and Lake Eyre South; an obvious outback draw (rule 1)
objection: A long linear feature, its stops are already separate candidates, and a pin on a line is arbitrary

name: Strzelecki Track
reason: Wikivoyage has its own article for the track, a remote route to Innamincka; one counted source and a drive, not a place to stop (rule 1,3)
objection: Equivalent to the Oodnadatta Track as a named outback route; against: remote, gravel and mostly a transit road

name: Anne Beadell Highway
reason: Remote 4WD desert route needing permits, mentioned in passing on the Stuart Highway page; no visitor stop (rule 2)
objection: A famous outback track; against: a one-line mention and most of it lies in another state

name: Painted Desert (South Australia)
reason: Wikivoyage Stuart Highway names the Painted Desert reached by AWD track from Cadney; coloured hills visitors go to, one source (rule 1)
objection: Real scenic draw; against: one passing mention, rough access, usually seen via tours or flights

name: Faye's Underground Home
reason: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy See listing: tour of a hand-dug underground home, open daily except Sunday, $5 (rule 2)
objection: Small family attraction; one counted source

name: Old Timers Mine
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: self-guided tour of a 1916 mine and underground homes, a signature Coober Pedy visit (rule 2)
objection: Wikivoyage link is marked dead; only one source

name: Tom's Working Opal Mine
reason: Wikivoyage calls it the pick of the working mines on Stuart Highway, but it is a tour operator; near-duplicate of the other mine visits
objection: It is a tour operator listing; for: a distinct working mine visit

name: Big Winch
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: lookout in the middle of Coober Pedy over the opal fields; a landmark Big Thing (rule 2,3)
objection: Short stop

name: Umoona Opal Mine and Museum
reason: southaustralia.com region page names it; underground mine, museum and dugout, a main Coober Pedy attraction (rule 2)
objection: Commercial business with accommodation; source is a region page

name: Saint Elijah the Prophet Serbian Orthodox Church
reason: Wikivoyage: church bored out of solid rock with a beautifully ornamented interior, a must see (church rule: interior named)
objection: Active church, may be restricted by services

name: Catholic Catacomb Church
reason: Wikivoyage names the Catholic church as a significant site but less intricate than the Serbian one; one source (church rule)
objection: For: underground interior a guide mentions; against: lesser than the Serbian church

name: Dingo Fence at Coober Pedy
reason: Wikivoyage Stuart Highway suggests a dirt-road trip 10 km to the Dingo Fence; landmark, one source
objection: For: iconic structure; against: a fence beside a road, 10 minute stop

name: Coober Pedy Mail Run
reason: Tour/vehicle operator, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place); link is dead
objection: A famous outback experience; against: an operator ride

name: Moon Plain
reason: southaustralia.com region page names the lunar-like plain and film location south of Coober Pedy; one counted source and a roadside look
objection: For: second-tier icon; against: a plain visited from a road, mostly seen by tour

name: Coober Pedy opal noodling fields
reason: An activity, not a distinct place; fossicking is covered by Coober Pedy tours and the mines (rule 3)
objection: Visitors do noodle; against: no single place or named site

name: Karkaroo (Andamooka Plesiosaur)
reason: Cannot confirm a public display place or visitor source describing where to see it (rule 1,2)
objection: Opalised fossil is a genuine curiosity

name: Lake Cadibarrawirracanna
reason: Remote salt lake with a passing mention only, no visitor facilities or description (rule 1,2)
objection: A large lake in the Arckaringa area

name: Woomera Missile Park
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: free open-air display of missiles and rockets in the town centre, with the Heritage Centre beside it (rule 2)
objection: Short stop of about 30 minutes

name: Woomera Heritage Centre
reason: Wikivoyage lists the Rocket Range Museum in the visitors' centre, about an hour, $6 (rule 2)
objection: Small museum; the History Museum next door may be a near duplicate

name: Woomera Obelisk
reason: Minor Australia Day monument beside the theatre (rule 3: minor memorial)
objection: Wikivoyage lists it

name: Deep Station 41
reason: One-line Wikivoyage mention of a former tracking facility 25 km south on range land; no visitor access or description (rule 2)
objection: Historic space-tracking site

name: Breen Park Bird Reserve
reason: Wikivoyage lists it with no description; local park in Woomera (rule 1,3)
objection: Wikivoyage names it

name: Spud's Roadhouse
reason: Roadhouse (restaurant/motel) at Pimba (rule 2)
objection: Quirky outback icon founded 1969 per Wikivoyage

name: Olympic Dam mine tour
reason: Operator tour of a mine (not a spot); the place is Roxby Downs/Olympic Dam, whose access is by booked tour only
objection: Large underground mine, a rare tourist tour

name: Roxby Downs Arid Recovery Reserve
reason: Fenced conservation reserve near Roxby Downs listed by flindersandoutback region page; open via tours, one source
objection: For: unique wildlife; against: access by tour only

name: Lake Torrens National Park
reason: Listed on flindersandoutback national parks page; huge salt lake park with no facilities and difficult access, one source
objection: For: a national park; against: remote and mostly inaccessible

name: Lake Gairdner National Park
reason: Wikivoyage Stuart Highway describes the third largest salt lake in Australia, used for speed records, with a national park beside the highway (rule 1)
objection: Access is hard to find, station-crossing and 4WD

name: Lake Hart
reason: southaustralia.com region page names the pink salt lake beside the Stuart Highway; a roadside stop travellers photograph
objection: Short roadside stop and sparse description

name: Marree Hotel
reason: Pub and accommodation business (rule 2)
objection: 1883 heritage building per Wikivoyage

name: Marree Mosque
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: recreation of Australia's first mosque built by Afghan cameleers (rule 2)
objection: Only a replica, short stop, mud-brick ruins

name: Marree Camel Cup
reason: Annual event, not a permanent place (rule 4)
objection: Famous event

name: Lake Eyre South
reason: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta Track side trip (3 km return) to Lake Eyre South; near-duplicate of Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre National Park (rule 3)
objection: For: easy roadside look at the lake; against: usually a dry salt flat and part of the larger lake

name: Anna Creek Painted Hills
reason: Seen by scenic flight only per source; a flight, not a place to visit (COVERAGE: spot is a place)
objection: Colourful hills

name: Curdimurka Siding
reason: Wikivoyage: preserved Ghan siding showing how settlers lived, one of the interesting sidings on the track (rule 2)
objection: Ruins and a sign, 20-minute stop

name: The Bubbler and Blanche Cup
reason: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta Track: the two best-known mound springs, a worthwhile diversion (rule 1,2)
objection: Overlaps Wabma Kadarbu Mound Springs Conservation Park

name: Wabma Kadarbu Mound Springs Conservation Park
reason: duplicate of The Bubbler and Blanche Cup (the park holds those springs; kept as one)
objection: Official park, could be the better kept entry

name: Coward Springs
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage (Oodnadatta Track) names the spa, historic rail siding, self-guided walk and camel safari; a second-tier Oodnadatta Track stop with things to do (opened).
objection: Mostly a campground; only one counted source and the Wabma Kadarbu mound springs nearby may be the real draw.

name: William Creek Hotel
reason: Rule 1: two counted sources (Flinders & Outback, Wikivoyage William Creek) call it one of the most remote pubs in the world; the pub is the landmark of William Creek, but it is a business (rule 2).
objection: For: famed remote-outback icon visitors photograph and stop at. Against: a pub/accommodation; William Creek town is the place and should carry it.

name: Algebuckina Bridge
reason: Rule 1+3: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta Track singles out the longest bridge in South Australia as a sight (opened); a named heritage roadside stop.
objection: One counted source, a short stop, and the Wikivoyage mention is a single clause.

name: Pink Roadhouse
reason: Rule 3 'quirky roadside icon': Wikivoyage Oodnadatta and Flinders & Outback both name the pink roadhouse as a feature of the town and the track's information hub (opened).
objection: It is a roadhouse/shop and fuel stop, which the business rule would reject; the case rests on its being a recognised landmark.

name: Railway Tjukurpa Museum
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta lists the preserved Ghan station museum, open daily 9-5 (opened).
objection: One counted source and a small-town museum with a short visit.

name: Angle Pole Memorial
reason: Rule 3: a minor memorial on the track; Wikivoyage mentions it in a single sentence with nothing to do.
objection: A named stop on the Oodnadatta Track marking the Overland Telegraph route.

name: Old Ghan Railway Heritage Trail
reason: Rule 2/3: a remote 4WD route branching off to Finke/Dalhousie, not a bounded place to visit; Wikivoyage gives no site.
objection: Heritage-trail branding suggests a promoted route.

name: Oodnadatta Races and Gymkhana
reason: Rule 4: annual event, not a permanent spot.
objection: None.

name: Munga-Thirri–Simpson Desert National Park
reason: Rule 1+2: Flinders & Outback national-parks page (opened) presents the Simpson Desert dunes as a headline 4WD destination; Desert Parks Pass, closed 1 Dec-15 Mar (note season).
objection: Very remote and permit-gated; many visitors will never enter, and it can be reached only by experienced 4WD travellers.

name: Witjira National Park
reason: Rule 1+2: Flinders & Outback outback page (opened) features Dalhousie Springs (swim in 37C artesian springs) and Mount Dare camping in Witjira.
objection: Remote and Desert Parks Pass required; Dalhousie Springs might be listed as its own spot, making the park a wrapper.

name: Purni Bore
reason: Rule 2/3: a campground and bore within Munga-Thirri; Flinders page lists it only as a camping spot.
objection: Wetland and bird hide near the bore could be a worthwhile stop.

name: 3 O'Clock Creek
reason: Rule 2/3: a campground inside Witjira; the source names it only as a camping spot.
objection: Flinders names it among the park's visitor facilities.

name: Simpson Desert Rocks Road
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage says the road may only be used in serious emergencies or with police permission; not a visitor attraction.
objection: None.

name: Malkumba–Coongie Lakes National Park
reason: Rule 1+2: Flinders & Outback park page (opened) calls it one of SA's most spectacular natural attractions: arid wetland, birds, canoeing; 4WD access. Keeps the Coongie Lakes duplicate as this one.
objection: About 100 km of 4WD tracks, access often impossible when wet or dry; few visitors in practice.

name: Coongie Lakes
reason: Duplicate of Malkumba–Coongie Lakes National Park (same wetland, kept under the park).
objection: Wikivoyage lists Coongie Lakes under See, and the lakes name is the one travellers use.

name: Innamincka Regional Reserve
reason: Rule 3: a protected area around Innamincka (Cooper Creek, Cullyamurra, Burke and Wills sites) named on the Flinders & Outback page (opened); an area rather than a sight, overlapping Cullyamurra and Cooper Creek.
objection: For: the park-managed reserve is where visitors camp, fish and cruise. Against: a reserve boundary, its attractions listed separately.

name: Cullyamurra Waterhole
reason: Rule 1+2: Flinders & Outback (opened) names Australia's largest billabong as a canoe/paddle destination on Cooper Creek, significant to the Traditional Owners.
objection: One counted source; remote and water-level dependent.

name: Dig Tree
reason: Outside the region: the Dig Tree stands in Queensland (Nockatunga), not South Australia, though Wikivoyage Innamincka suggests a day drive.
objection: A major Burke and Wills icon visitors from Innamincka go to; another region's app would hold it.

name: Innamincka Town Sunset Lookout
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Innamincka See lists a sunset lookout 1 km NE of town; no description beyond its location.
objection: For: named in the town's See list. Against: a short viewpoint with no description, one source.

name: Burke and Wills Memorial at Innamincka
reason: Rule 1/3: neither source lists a specific memorial or site; they mention the expedition's deaths on Cooper Creek only as history (re-checked Wikivoyage and Flinders page).
objection: Burke and Wills site and Howitt's Grave are a real visitor draw near the town; the sources just did not name it as such.

name: Cooper Creek
reason: Rule 3: a long river, not a bounded place; its visitor sites (Cullyamurra, Crossing, Reserve) are separate candidates.
objection: Two counted sources name the creek with cruises and fishing.

name: Innamincka Hotel
reason: Rule 2: pub and accommodation (a business); Innamincka town is the place.
objection: Two counted sources feature the hotel as the town's hub.

name: Queerbidie Waterhole
reason: Rule 1/3: one Wikivoyage line, 'one of two significant waterholes', with nothing to see or do described.
objection: Waterholes are the main natural sights near Innamincka.

name: Innamincka Station
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage itself says it is on private land.
objection: None.

name: Strzelecki Regional Reserve
reason: Rule 3: a large reserve area; the Wikivoyage Strzelecki Track page does not list it as a stop.
objection: Named in the reserve context for dunes and lakes.

name: Mount Hopeless
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage lists it only as a waypoint ('Oh poor you, have some hope'), with nothing to see or do.
objection: A named landmark of the Strzelecki Track visitors photograph at the sign.

name: Moomba
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage says it is a company town closed to non-employees with no services.
objection: None.

name: Merty Merty
reason: Rule 1/2: listed only as a waypoint with no description; a station settlement.
objection: Named on the track page.

name: Lake Harry Ruins and Clayton Station
reason: Rule 1: the cited Wikivoyage National Route 83 page (re-read) does not mention it; no counted source names it.
objection: Real historic ruins on the Birdsville Track.

name: Tirari Desert
reason: Rule 3: a desert region crossed by a road, not a place; the cited page does not name it.
objection: Dune country is a draw in itself.

name: Cooper Creek Crossing
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Innamincka Do lists the causeway, with pelicans at the culverts in the evening; short stop in town.
objection: For: named Do item, free, easy, wildlife. Against: one source, a causeway within walking distance of the town.

name: Mulka Ruins
reason: Rule 1: the cited Wikivoyage National Route 83 page (re-read) does not mention Mulka; no counted source names it.
objection: Real historic ruins on the Birdsville Track.

name: Witchelina Nature Reserve
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source found; visits since 2026 are Nature Foundation members only, with bookings and fees (re-searched).
objection: 421,000 ha reserve with nature drives and walks; Wikipedia article exists.

name: Kalamurina Sanctuary
reason: Rule 1/2: AWC's own visiting page (opened) allows pre-booked tours (Outback Spirit) and booked self-drive visits, up to five vehicles, April-October; no tourism-board source.
objection: For: significant wildlife sanctuary at the Warburton/Lake Eyre inflow. Against: booking-only, tours, operator source only, access depends on road conditions.

name: Lake Frome National Park
reason: Outside the region: belongs to sa-flinders (reached from Balcanoona in Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges); also no counted source found in this pass.
objection: A salt lake national park with a 4WD track from Gammon Ranges.

name: Elizabeth Symon Nursing Home
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Innamincka See lists the heritage-listed former nursing home, once a park interpretive centre, now Parks HQ; unclear whether it is open to visitors.
objection: For: heritage-register building and the place to find rangers. Against: now a park office, one source, no stated public access.

name: Starlight Cinema Innamincka
reason: Rule 2/4: an outdoor cinema run by the hotel, a business; not a permanent attraction.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as a Do item.

name: Cooper Creek Tours Innamincka
reason: Operator, not a place.
objection: None.
